flagged.evidence: The file identifies https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01X8 as 'Cohomology of Schemes, Section 30.10' and its locator attributes the scheme-level stabilization statement to that target. Opening the URL shows Section 30.2, 'Čech cohomology of quasi-coherent sheaves', which does not contain that statement. The actual stabilization result is [Stacks Lemma 30.10.1, tag 01Y8](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01Y8); its statement and complete proof were checked. The item's independent affine-cover proof remains sound, but the second citation is inaccurate.

The opening asserts finite point-blowup resolution on 'an arbitrary regular surface', assuming only finite normalization of each curve component. The cited theorem instead states: 'Let S be a regular surface: a Noetherian scheme of pure dimension two all of whose local rings are regular.' The scoped SNC definition allows locally Noetherian surfaces, so Noetherianity is not implicit in that terminology. Counterexample: take S to be a countably infinite disjoint union of affine planes over Q and Z the disjoint union of cusps y^2=x^3, one in each plane. S is a locally Noetherian regular surface of pure dimension two, Z is a reduced curve, and every component has finite normalization. Finitely many blowups at individual closed points affect only finitely many connected components, leaving infinitely many singular cusps; consequently the final support cannot be SNC. The opening needs the theorem's Noetherian hypothesis.
